title: Distribution, Research, and Pricing - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Pricing
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the primary nature of the pricing function in a business?
options: To ensure products look appealing on the shelf
To establish the value of a product or service in monetary terms to generate revenue
To determine how products will be transported
To write the advertising copy for the marketing campaign
questions.explain: Pricing determines the exchange value of a good or service. It is the only component of the marketing mix that directly generates revenue and profits.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A tech company releases a brand-new, innovative smartphone and sets the initial price very high to recover research and development costs before competitors enter the market. What pricing strategy is this?
questions.explain: Price skimming involves setting a high initial price for a new or highly demanded product and lowering it over time as competition increases.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A new streaming service enters the market with a very low initial monthly fee to attract a large number of subscribers quickly and build market share. This strategy is known as:
questions.explain: Penetration pricing sets an artificially low initial price to capture market share rapidly and create brand loyalty before eventually raising the price.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: According to the economic principles of supply and demand, what typically happens to the price of a product if consumer demand is very high but the supply is very low?
options: The price will stay the same.
questions.explain: When demand exceeds supply (a shortage), producers can generally raise prices because consumers are willing to pay more to acquire the limited good.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A business determines its product price by calculating the total cost of producing the item and then adding a specific percentage to that cost for profit. What is this pricing method called?
questions.explain: Cost-plus pricing (or markup pricing) involves adding a standard markup percentage to the cost of producing or acquiring the product.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When a change in the price of a product results in a very significant change in consumer demand, the demand for that product is said to be:
questions.explain: Elastic demand means consumers are highly sensitive to price changes. Small changes in price lead to significant changes in the quantity demanded.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following products is most likely to have inelastic demand?
questions.explain: Inelastic demand occurs when price changes do not significantly affect the quantity demanded. Necessities and life-saving medicines usually have highly inelastic demand.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is an illegal practice where competitors secretly agree to set the same prices for their products to avoid competition?
questions.explain: Price fixing is an illegal, anti-competitive practice where rival companies agree to artificially maintain prices at a certain level.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Selling the exact same product to different buyers at different prices, under similar circumstances, is generally known as:
questions.explain: Price discrimination involves charging different customers different prices for the same product. While sometimes legal (like student discounts), it is illegal in B2B contexts if it harms competition under laws like the Robinson-Patman Act.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A grocery store sells a staple item like milk slightly below its cost to attract customers into the store, hoping they will buy other, more profitable items. This milk is functioning as a:
questions.explain: A loss leader is a pricing strategy where a product is sold at a price below its market cost to stimulate other sales of more profitable goods.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: The point at which total revenues exactly equal total costs, resulting in zero profit but also zero loss, is known as the:
questions.explain: The break-even point is reached when a business sells enough units at a specific price to cover all fixed and variable costs.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Setting prices at $9.99 instead of $10.00 to make the price seem lower to the consumer relies on what concept?
questions.explain: Psychological pricing (specifically odd-even pricing) uses consumer psychology to make a price appear significantly cheaper because the left-most digit is lower.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What pricing strategy involves combining several products and offering them at a single price that is usually lower than if the items were purchased separately?
questions.explain: Bundle pricing groups multiple products together as a package deal, offering perceived value to the customer while often increasing the seller's total revenue.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: How do fixed costs differ from variable costs when determining a pricing strategy?
options: Fixed costs change based on the number of products produced, while variable costs stay the same.
Fixed costs stay the same regardless of production volume, while variable costs change with production volume.
Fixed costs only apply to marketing, whereas variable costs apply only to production.
Fixed costs are optional expenses, while variable costs are mandatory.
questions.explain: Fixed costs (like rent or salaries) do not fluctuate with production levels. Variable costs (like raw materials) increase directly with the amount of product produced.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A hotel chain uses software to adjust room rates hourly based on current demand, local events, and competitor pricing. What type of pricing is this?
questions.explain: Dynamic pricing involves highly flexible prices for products or services based on current market demands, algorithms, and real-time conditions.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: High-end brands like Rolex and Gucci intentionally keep their prices very high to convey an image of exclusivity, luxury, and superior quality. This strategy is known as:
questions.explain: Prestige pricing is the practice of pricing goods at a high level to give the appearance of quality and status.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: During the 'maturity' stage of a product's life cycle, what is a typical pricing strategy?
options: Pricing very high because it is a novelty
Pricing competitively to maintain market share as competition is high
Significantly increasing prices because demand has just begun
questions.explain: In the maturity stage, competition is at its peak. Companies generally use competitive pricing, discounts, and promotions to defend their market share against rivals.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A retailer advertises a deeply discounted television to lure customers into the store. When customers arrive, the retailer claims the item is sold out and heavily pressures them to buy a much more expensive model. This deceptive practice is called:
questions.explain: Bait-and-switch is an unethical and often illegal practice where a 'bait' (a low-priced item) is advertised but the seller intends to switch the buyer to a higher-priced item.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When a firm sets its pricing objective specifically to achieve a certain percentage of profit over its expenses, this goal is called:
questions.explain: Target ROI pricing is a profit-oriented goal where prices are calculated to generate a specific desired percentage return relative to the investment.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Value-based pricing depends primarily on:
options: The production cost of the item
The buyer's perception of the product's worth or benefits
The legally mandated maximum price set by the government
The exact price charged by the nearest competitor
questions.explain: Value-based pricing sets prices largely on the consumer's perceived value of the product or service, rather than on the strict cost of production.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
